facts.fact: The BCEAO launched the PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform on 30 September 2025 and, from 2 November 2026, sets that interoperable transfers between wallets, banks and other institutions go through it with fee caps, per APA.

MLI.note: PI-SPI is regional; not a PAPSS fact.
Fee caps are tariff rules; no consumer protection body or rule stated.

facts.fact: APA says fourteen Malian institutions were authorised to open PI-SPI services to the public per a September 2026 list, including BNDA, BDM, Ecobank, Coris Bank and Orange Finances Mobiles Mali.

MLI.note: Cross-country tariff alignment is planned for 1 June 2027.

facts.fact: New BCEAO rules on fees and wallet limits for e-money transfers apply in Mali from 2 November 2026, per APA.
APA says interoperable transfers from wallets to banks, e-money institutions, microfinance institutions or payment institutions must now go through PI-SPI.

MLI.note: The 61.9% is a rate of use of financial services, not a share of adults with an account.

facts.fact: Mali's wallet-to-bank and wallet-to-wallet transfers run through PI-SPI from 2 November 2026, with Orange Money and BNDA customers named as using it, per APA.

MLI.note: PI-SPI is regional, so no national switch fact.
